publicationMetadataPlan.mediaDescription: No generated media; these conditional clinical-caution pages do not resolve a single non-prescriptive physical subject, agent, protocol, evidence state, or claim boundary
publicationMetadataPlan.sourceUse: Current controlled records, public-health guidance, and local source-resolution evidence define asset-free scientific holds.

controlFinalReview.reviewer: WikiBiome Control Tower clinical safety, scientific, source-resolution, and editorial audit

reviewStandard: Clinical-caution pages may not receive generic warning graphics, stop-sign imagery, implied treatment-withholding scenes, invented products, or a disease image that could be mistaken for evidence supporting the page's recommendation. All six routes fail before prompt creation.
promotionRule: No Batch 114 source hash exists or is eligible for promotion. All six routes remain asset-free scientific holds. No generated source, master, derivative, registry record, endpoint, Schema object, social preview, or image-sitemap entry may be created from this batch.

routeDecisions.reason: The page is a conditional treatment caution, not a stable physical entity. It does not select an antibacterial agent, pathogen, indication, route, dose, timing, chemotherapy regimen, neutropenia state, or patient context, and both local source identifiers carry unresolved `.md` suffixes. An ovary, tumor, infusion, pill, microbiome, or crossed-out treatment scene would imply that antibiotic therapy should be withheld and could conceal the page's life-threatening-infection exception.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Repair the source identifiers; reconcile the title and claims to current clinical guidance; define agent, pathogen, documented-infection criteria, spectrum, route, dose, timing, chemotherapy regimen, neutropenia state, population, comparator, outcomes, and emergency exceptions; then identify a non-prescriptive subject that cannot be mistaken for a treatment directive.

routeDecisions.reason: The two linked sources address mouse arsenic toxicology and ZIP8-associated metal dyshomeostasis rather than a clinical broad-spectrum-antibiotic protocol in Crohn disease. The route does not select a drug, infection, disease phenotype, dose, duration, population, comparator, outcome, or abscess/fistula exception. A gut, capsule, bacterium, microbiome-loss, or prohibition scene would turn mechanistic speculation into a visual treatment recommendation.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Add direct clinical evidence and current guideline context; select the exact antibacterial class or agent, indication, pathogen, Crohn phenotype, infection or complication state, dose, route, duration, population, comparator, endpoints, harms, and exceptions; then define a non-prescriptive visual subject.

routeDecisions.reason: The page spans unspecified broad-spectrum agents, several taxa, biofilms, antimicrobial resistance, metal co-resistance, autoimmunity, butyrate biology, and multiple proposed alternatives. Dysbiosis itself is compositional and context-dependent. One ecological or microbial scene would invent a baseline, taxonomic composition, treatment effect, and causal direction; a crossed-out pill would be prescriptive.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Select an exact agent or regimen, indication, microbiome compartment, baseline composition, assay, time points, population, comparator, measured ecological effects, clinical outcomes, and exceptions, and resolve the proposed alternatives to direct evidence before designing any non-prescriptive media.

routeDecisions.reason: The only linked study concerns antibiotic-treated acute COVID-19 patients with translocation and bacteremia, while the route makes a Long COVID treatment caution. It does not select an agent, documented bacterial infection, symptom phenotype, dose, duration, population, comparator, microbiome assay, endpoint, or safety boundary. Lung, virus, bacterium, pill, or microbiome imagery would conflate acute infection, post-acute disease, and antibiotic indication.

routeDecisions.reason: The route combines dietary calcium, multiple supplement compounds and sources, cadmium exposure, transport mechanisms, bone and kidney outcomes, product contamination, and clinical monitoring. Current ATSDR material notes that calcium may reduce cadmium toxicity in deficient individuals while not recommending clinical use for adequately nourished people; the page's categorical STOP framing cannot be represented by one calcium, cadmium, tablet, bone, kidney, or transporter scene without implying a treatment rule or an unmeasured contaminated product.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Reconcile the clinical claim with current toxicology guidance; select exact calcium compound, formulation, product and lot, measured cadmium content and method, exposure matrix, dose, population, baseline calcium status, renal state, comparator, monitoring, thresholds, outcomes, contraindications, and tested-product provenance before any media audit.

routeDecisions.reason: This page describes an epistemic and regulatory caution about interpreting discovery-phase pancreatic-cancer microbiome associations. Its four studies use different bacterial, fungal, Mendelian-randomization, and observational designs. A pancreas, microbial panel, specimen tube, ROC curve, or diagnostic-device scene would imply a defined validated assay, cutoff, performance estimate, or cleared product that the page explicitly says does not exist.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Define a specific assay, specimen, pre-analytic protocol, feature set, validation cohort, prespecified cutoff, sensitivity, specificity, intended-use population, comparator, regulatory status, and versioned evidence state. Until then, use editorial interface treatment rather than scientific primary media.
